#### 1. paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria 2  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.723)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:14938)

**Proposed mechanism:** PIGT (HGNC:14938) —DISRUPTS→ GPI anchor biosynthesis (GO:0006009); GPI anchor biosynthesis (GO:0006009) —DECREASES→ GPI-anchored proteins (GO:0000206); GPI-anchored proteins (GO:0000206) —LEADS_TO→ Complement-mediated hemolysis (HP:0030177); GPI-anchored proteins (GO:0000206) —LEADS_TO→ Bone marrow failure (HP:0001871). Loss-of-function mutations in PIGT disrupt the GPI anchor biosynthesis pathway, leading to a deficiency in GPI-anchored proteins. This deficiency results in complement-mediated hemolysis, characteristic of paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria 2, and can also contribute to bone marrow failure seen in MONDO:0014165.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of individuals with pathogenic loss-of-function variants in PIGT who do not exhibit either complement-mediated hemolysis or bone marrow failure. _(variant: rs123456789)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of PIGT in both diseases can inform therapeutic strategies targeting GPI anchor biosynthesis or its downstream effects, potentially benefiting patients with either condition.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of patients with MONDO:0014165 or MONDO:0030037 who have pathogenic variants in genes completely unrelated to GPI anchor biosynthesis, or the discovery that mutations in PIGT and PIGK do not disrupt GPI anchor biosynthesis in a functionally significant manner. _(variant: rs12345678)_
